one_liner: Media relations and communications specialist at CBP headquarters: handling press inquiries, writing releases and statements, planning media events, and advising field offices on public affairs.
fit_summary: Daniel's people skills, policy knowledge, and government-client consulting at IEM fit public affairs work well, but GS-12 requires one year of specialized experience managing media and public communications, writing press releases and advisories, and advising staff on media coverage. Unless Daniel's IEM role, or prior or volunteer work such as campaigns or advocacy, included real media relations and communications products, Daniel will likely be found ineligible. If Daniel does have that experience, this becomes a Good fit.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no federal status needed. The fed-transition path is for CTAP/ICTAP eligibles, and Daniel does not qualify for that path.

One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-11: managing media and public communications, developing press releases and media advisories, advising field offices and staff on media coverage, and planning communication strategies. The resume must state this explicitly.
U.S. residency for at least 3 of the last 5 years, plus Selective Service registration if applicable.
A CBP law-enforcement-level background investigation, including questions on drug use and felonies, plus drug testing. No security clearance is required.
You must complete the USA Hire online assessment and meet its cut score.
strategy: Before investing time, honestly check whether Daniel has a full year (stated as total hours per week) of media and public communications work. If not, target GS-9/11 public affairs or communications roles, or Virginia state and local PIO roles, instead.

Frame the IEM experience around any public information or communications tasks you actually did for government clients, such as emergency public messaging, preparedness outreach, stakeholder briefings, or communication plans. Use the posting's exact wording.
Keep the resume to two pages. Each job should list dates, hours per week, and a tight specialized-experience section that mirrors the four duty statements in the posting.
Preview the questionnaire at the posted link before applying, and answer 'expert' only where your resume shows evidence to back it up. Overstating can remove you from consideration.
The window is only October 27 to November 2, 2026. Draft the resume beforehand, apply early, and schedule the USA Hire assessment right away, preparing for its reasoning and reading items.
Include campaign, legislative, or volunteer communications work if you have it, since volunteer experience counts.
resume_bullets: Drafted [number] [news releases/media advisories/public statements] on [emergency management/disaster recovery topic] for [government client], coordinating review with [stakeholders] under [deadline/sensitivity constraints].
Developed and implemented communication plans for [program/event], tracking [metric, e.g., media pickups or engagement] to measure communication performance and adjust messaging.
Advised [client field staff/officials] on responding to [media/public/stakeholder inquiries] during [disaster or exercise], and prepared [talking points/Q&A] to ensure accurate representation.
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you handled a sensitive or controversial media inquiry. How did you protect information that couldn't be released?
Walk us through how you'd build a communication plan for a new CBP program, and how you'd measure whether it worked.
How would you advise a field office facing negative local coverage of an operation?
Describe working under a tight deadline with multiple reviewers on an official statement.
watch_outs: Specialized experience is the major hurdle. Without documented media and press work at a GS-11-equivalent level, you will be rated ineligible.
The application window is very short (closes November 2, 2026), and the USA Hire cut score is pass/fail.
The job is on-site only, with no telework, in DC. That means a long commute from Manassas, though VRE is an option.
CBP is a law-enforcement agency with an intensive background check and drug testing, and the work involves politically sensitive immigration and border messaging.
